name: Kokoro-82M
tagline: 82M params, Apache 2.0, runs on a potato

editorial.good_for: Excellent quality. Tiny model. Runs almost anywhere.

about: Kokoro is an 82-million-parameter text-to-speech model that consistently punches far above its weight, topping community TTS leaderboards against models many times its size. It ships with a set of polished preset voices and is fast enough to run in real time on modest hardware — which makes it even faster behind a hosted API.
best_for: Lightweight narration and app voices when preset voices are enough.
limitations: No voice cloning. Language and voice quality vary; test names, numbers, and longer passages.
hardware_notes: CPU inference is supported. Speed depends on processor, text length, and runtime; the old speed estimate is not a standardized benchmark.
quickstart:
# Install system dependency espeak-ng if required by your OS.
# pip install kokoro soundfile
from kokoro import KPipeline
import soundfile as sf
pipeline = KPipeline(lang_code="a")
for i, (_, _, audio) in enumerate(pipeline("Hello from OpenSpeech.", voice="af_bella")):
    sf.write(f"speech-{i}.wav", audio, 24000)

name: Chatterbox
tagline: English voice cloning with emotion-exaggeration controls

editorial.good_for: An English voice-cloning baseline with MIT-licensed weights.

about: Chatterbox is Resemble AI's open-source TTS model — a 0.5B-parameter system with zero-shot voice cloning from a few seconds of reference audio and a unique emotion-exaggeration control. In blind tests it's frequently preferred over leading commercial systems. Outputs include Resemble's PerTh watermark.
best_for: English voice cloning with controllable exaggeration.
limitations: This page represents the original English model. Turbo and Multilingual V3 are separate releases; samples here are not V3.

name: XTTS v2
tagline: Voice cloning from a short reference clip across 17 languages

editorial.pitch: The most-downloaded TTS on Hugging Face for a reason.

about: XTTS v2 is the flagship model of the Coqui TTS framework and one of the most widely used open voice-cloning models ever released. It clones a voice from a ~6-second sample and speaks 17 languages, with cross-language cloning — record in English, speak in Japanese. Coqui the company shut down, but the model remains a community staple.
best_for: Cross-language cloning from a short reference recording.
limitations: The weights use CPML with non-commercial restrictions. Review the model license before choosing it for a product.
hardware_notes: The catalog’s 6 GB figure is a rough historical estimate, not a measured minimum. CUDA is useful for practical inference; follow the maintained Coqui TTS instructions.
quickstart:
# Use the Python environment described in the Coqui documentation.
# Provide a clean reference clip that you have permission to use.
from TTS.api import TTS
tts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to("cuda")
tts.tts_to_file(text="Hello from OpenSpeech.",
    speaker_wav="reference.wav", language="en", file_path="speech.wav")

name: Fish Speech 1.5
tagline: Earlier Fish Speech voice-cloning model; compare with S2 Pro

editorial.pitch: Benchmarks above closed-source models on multilingual quality.

about: These recordings were generated with Fish Speech 1.5. Fish Audio S2 Pro is a separate release with different weights and licensing. Keep this page for comparing the original samples.
best_for: Comparing earlier Fish Speech recordings with newer releases.
limitations: Historical sample set. Check the exact 1.5 code and weight licenses; current repository instructions target S2 Pro.

name: Piper
tagline: Tiny, fast, runs offline on a Raspberry Pi
about: Piper is the workhorse of local text-to-speech — built by the Rhasspy voice-assistant project to run in real time on devices as small as a Raspberry Pi. It offers a huge catalog of community voices across dozens of languages. Through the API you get the same dependable output without managing voice files or ONNX runtimes. The original MIT-licensed rhasspy/piper repo is archived; the actively maintained fork is OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl, licensed GPL-3.0.
quickstart:
python -m piper.download_voices en_US-ljspeech-medium
python -m piper -m en_US-ljspeech-medium.onnx -f output.wav -- "Hello from OpenSpeech."
limitations: The current Piper engine uses GPL-3.0; each voice has its own terms. These recordings use the public-domain LJ Speech dataset voice. Older Rhasspy engine releases used MIT.
hardware_notes: These samples were generated on an Apple Silicon CPU. No cross-model speed benchmark is claimed.

name: Bark
tagline: Generates laughter, sighs, and music — the chaotic one

editorial.pitch: The chaotic one — generates laughter, sighs, even music. Use with intention.

about: Bark, from Suno, is a generative text-to-audio model rather than a plain TTS system. Beyond multilingual speech it produces laughter, sighs, crying, music, and background sounds from inline cues — trading precise control for creative range. Still unmatched for character and chaos.

name: F5-TTS
tagline: Flow-matching TTS, fast zero-shot voice cloning

editorial.pitch: Fast, flow-matched voice cloning. Zero-shot from a short reference.

about: F5-TTS uses flow matching with a diffusion transformer to produce fluent, faithful zero-shot voice clones from a single short reference. It became a community favorite for its simple architecture, fast inference, and surprisingly robust cloning quality. The official pretrained weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial); a community retrain called OpenF5-TTS is Apache-licensed for commercial use.

name: Parler-TTS
tagline: Describe the voice in natural language ('soft female, fast, clear')
about: Parler-TTS, from Hugging Face's audio team, takes a different approach: instead of cloning a reference, you describe the speaker in text — "a calm female voice with a slight British accent, speaking slowly" — and it synthesizes that voice. Fully open training code and data recipes.

name: Dia
tagline: Ultra-realistic two-speaker dialogue, sounds like a podcast

editorial.pitch: Sounds like a podcast — two-speaker dialogue out of the box.

about: Dia generates full conversations directly from screenplay-style text — tag lines with [S1] and [S2] and it renders a natural two-voice dialogue in a single pass, complete with laughs, coughs, and throat-clears. A 1.6B model that went viral for podcast-style output rivaling paid tools. Nari Labs released Dia2 in November 2025.

name: CosyVoice 2
tagline: Alibaba's real-time TTS, 150ms streaming latency
about: CosyVoice 2 from Alibaba's FunAudioLLM team is engineered for real-time use: streaming synthesis at roughly 150ms first-packet latency with quality nearly identical to offline mode. It supports zero-shot cloning, cross-lingual synthesis, dialect control, and natural-language instructions over emotion and style. CosyVoice 3, a newer 0.5B Apache-2.0 model in the same family, has since been released.

name: IndexTTS 2
tagline: Bilibili's TTS with multi-speaker and precise emotion control
about: IndexTTS 2, from Bilibili, targets professional dubbing: it's the rare autoregressive TTS with explicit duration control (hit an exact clip length) and disentangled emotion control — take the voice from one reference and the emotion from another, or steer it with text.

name: VibeVoice
tagline: Microsoft's long-form TTS — 90 minutes, 4 speakers
about: VibeVoice is Microsoft's long-form TTS: it can synthesize up to ~90 minutes of continuous audio with up to four distinct speakers in a single generation — built for podcast-style content. Ultra-low-frame-rate tokenizers keep generation efficient despite the scale.

name: Qwen3-TTS
tagline: Alibaba's flagship, 97ms latency, 10 languages
about: Qwen3-TTS is the text-to-speech line from Alibaba's Qwen team, known for strong multilingual coverage — including Chinese dialects like Cantonese, Wu, and Sichuanese — with expressive preset voices and fast synthesis backed by the Qwen model family.
best_for: Multilingual preset voices, voice design, and cloning across model variants.
limitations: CustomVoice, VoiceDesign, and Base checkpoints provide different capabilities. The demo uses the English Serena preset.

name: Orpheus TTS
tagline: Llama-3 based, empathetic, low-latency for interactive apps

editorial.good_for: Llama-3 based. Empathetic. Built for interactive apps.

about: Orpheus is a Llama-3B-based speech model from Canopy Labs. It generates remarkably human intonation and supports inline emotive tags like laughter and sighs, plus zero-shot voice cloning and low-latency streaming. One of the most natural conversational voices in open source.
best_for: Expressive English dialogue with preset voices and emotion tags.
limitations: These samples use the English 3B 0.1 fine-tune. Other language releases are separate checkpoints. Local inference has a heavier GPU setup than Kokoro.
hardware_notes: The catalog’s 12 GB figure is an estimate. Follow the author’s vLLM and CUDA requirements for the chosen checkpoint.

name: KittenTTS
tagline: 15M params, under 25MB, runs anywhere — even your phone
about: KittenTTS is an ultra-lightweight English TTS model — around 15 million parameters, small enough to run without a GPU entirely. It trades some expressiveness for extreme efficiency, with a handful of clean preset voices. Via the API it's effectively instant.

name: OpenVoice v2
tagline: Tone-color cloning + cross-lingual transfer
about: OpenVoice v2 clones the tone color of a reference speaker and then lets you control style — emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses, intonation — independently. It supports cross-lingual cloning into languages the reference speaker never spoke, and v2 moved to a permissive MIT license.

name: StyleTTS 2
tagline: Diffusion-based, human-level naturalness on LibriTTS
about: StyleTTS 2 made waves by reaching human-level naturalness on standard English benchmarks using style diffusion and adversarial training with large speech-language models. It supports zero-shot speaker adaptation from a short reference clip and remains a favorite for natural prosody.

name: MeloTTS
tagline: Multilingual, real-time on CPU
about: MeloTTS from MyShell.ai is one of the most-downloaded open TTS models on Hugging Face. It covers English (with multiple accents), Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, and was designed for real-time inference even on CPU. A clean, dependable choice for multilingual products.

name: Spark-TTS
tagline: Built on Qwen2.5, zero-shot voice cloning + style control
about: Spark-TTS builds speech generation directly on a 0.5B Qwen backbone with a single-stream codec, making it unusually simple and efficient. It does zero-shot cloning plus controllable voice creation — set gender, pitch, and speaking style to synthesize a new voice from scratch.

name: MegaTTS 3
tagline: ByteDance's TTS with sparse alignment — robust prosody
about: MegaTTS 3 is ByteDance's open release: a compact 0.45B diffusion-transformer TTS with high-quality zero-shot cloning, bilingual Chinese/English support with code-switching, and unusual extras like adjustable accent intensity for pronunciation control.

name: WhisperSpeech
tagline: Whisper, but inverted — TTS by 'unwrapping' OpenAI's ASR
about: WhisperSpeech, from Collabora, flips OpenAI's Whisper architecture around to generate speech instead of transcribing it. It's trained entirely on properly licensed open data — a deliberately transparent, commercially safe stack — with voice cloning from reference audio.

name: Higgs Audio v2
tagline: Built on Llama 3.2 3B, 10M+ hours of training audio
about: Higgs Audio v2 builds audio generation on top of a Llama-3-class language model trained on 10M+ hours of audio. It wins the majority of emotion benchmarks against leading commercial models and does things few others can: multi-speaker dialogue, melodic humming, and voice cloning with deep prosody understanding. Higgs Audio v3 (4B params) moved to a non-commercial research license, so v2 remains the recommended open pick.

name: GPT-SoVITS
tagline: The community's favorite few-shot voice-cloning toolkit
about: GPT-SoVITS has one of the largest communities in open voice AI. It does zero-shot cloning from a few seconds of audio, but its signature trick is few-shot training: with just one minute of a voice it produces a dramatically more faithful clone. That workflow made it the de facto standard for hobbyist voice cloning, especially across the Chinese and Japanese communities.

name: Sesame CSM-1B
tagline: The conversational speech model behind the viral Maya demo
about: CSM-1B is the open model from Sesame, whose 'Maya' assistant demo went viral for sounding uncannily present — breath, hesitation, tone shifts and all. It generates speech conditioned on conversation context, so replies sound like part of a dialogue rather than isolated lines. The open release is the base generation model behind that demo.

name: Zonos
tagline: 44kHz studio-quality output with emotion control
about: Zonos from Zyphra generates native 44kHz audio — noticeably crisper than the 22-24kHz most open models produce — with zero-shot cloning from a short reference and explicit control over emotions like happiness, sadness, and anger. It ships in both pure-transformer and SSM-hybrid variants.

name: NeuTTS Air
tagline: On-device-class TTS with instant cloning from ~3 seconds
about: NeuTTS Air from Neuphonic is built to run in real time on a CPU — a ~0.7B-parameter model on a Qwen backbone that still manages instant voice cloning from around three seconds of reference audio. It's designed for on-device privacy, which also makes it one of the cheapest modern TTS models to serve.

name: Step-Audio-EditX
tagline: Re-edit the emotion or style of audio you already generated
about: Step-Audio-EditX from StepFun AI is built around iterative editing rather than one-shot generation: you can take audio you already made and regenerate just the emotion, style, or a paralinguistic detail (breathing, laughter) without touching the words or re-cloning the voice. It tops recent open-model Elo rankings for emotion control, and also handles Cantonese and Sichuanese dialects alongside standard Mandarin and English.

name: Kyutai TTS
tagline: Word-level streaming TTS built for live voice agents
about: Kyutai TTS pairs a 1B backbone with a 600M depth transformer to stream audio at the word level, generating 12.5Hz frames fast enough for real-time conversational agents. Voice cloning is deliberately disabled — it only speaks from a fixed set of precomputed voice embeddings, a safety choice that trades flexibility for guardrails against impersonation.

name: Maya1
tagline: Design a voice from a text description, not a reference clip
about: Maya1 from Maya Research skips voice cloning entirely: you describe the voice you want in natural language and it designs one from scratch, with over 20 inline emotion tags — laugh, sigh, whisper, and more — for expressive delivery. Served through vLLM it hits sub-100ms latency, making it viable for live, interactive use.

name: SoulX-Podcast
tagline: Multi-speaker podcast dialogue with dialect support
about: SoulX-Podcast, built on Qwen3 by Soul AI Lab, generates multi-speaker, multi-turn podcast dialogue in a single pass, complete with paralinguistics like laughter. It supports cross-dialect voice cloning across Sichuanese, Henanese, and Cantonese alongside standard Mandarin and English.

name: Muyan-TTS
tagline: Full training code released, trained for ~$50K on podcast audio
about: Muyan-TTS from MYZY-AI is a LLaMA-3.2-3B-based pipeline trained on more than 100,000 hours of podcast audio for a total training cost of around $50,000. Unusually for open TTS, MYZY-AI released the full training code, not just inference — letting anyone reproduce or fine-tune the pipeline from scratch.

name: Voxtral TTS
tagline: Mistral's zero-shot cloning model, ~70ms latency across 9 languages
about: Voxtral TTS is Mistral AI's Ministral-3B-based speech model, cloning a voice from just 3 seconds of reference audio and streaming it back in roughly 70ms — fast enough for live agents — across nine languages. The weights are non-commercial; commercial use requires a separate agreement with Mistral.

name: Llasa
tagline: LLM-native TTS built straight on the Llama architecture
about: Llasa from HKUST Audio is an LLM-native TTS model — it runs the unmodified Llama architecture over XCodec2 speech tokens instead of bolting on a separate audio decoder, and does zero-shot voice cloning from a short reference. It ships in 1B, 3B, and 8B variants, trading size for fidelity.
